target_customer: Consumers and professionals overloaded with information across email, social and cloud accounts
problem: Personal data was scattered across Gmail, Facebook, Dropbox and more. Greplin indexed those accounts for search, then as Cue surfaced relevant information for the day.
business_model: Freemium consumer search with a paid tier for professional accounts and heavy data

founders.name: Daniel Gross
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no background.

founders.name: Robby Walker
founders.background_notes: YC page: later spent about nine years at Apple leading Siri and Information Intelligence.

founders.name: Shai Magzimof
founders.background_notes: YC page and Wikipedia list him; YC page lists later startups (Nextpeer, Phantom Auto) only.

competitors.name: Xobni
competitors.what: Outlook and Gmail contact and email search add-on

competitors.name: Introspectr
competitors.what: Social search startup in the same space

technical_complexity.rationale: Indexing private data from many APIs with authorization, near real time sync and fast search, built by a handful of engineers.

defensibility.rationale: TechCrunch noted Google or someone else could build similar search; value depended on third party API access that could change.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google did not ship a direct clone in the sources found. Apple acquired Cue in October 2013, and Cue shut down its service.

market_need_then: Users spread data across many online services in 2010 and TechCrunch reported strong early interest; the sources give no spend figures.

branding.domain_note: Greplin used greplin.com; Cue used cueup.com, which returned HTTP 503 on fetch.

rebrands.why: Repositioned from search to a personal assistant app; the rationale for the name was not found

brand_strength.rationale: Greplin had press attention as a personal search engine and the Cue rename was a deliberate reposition, but no source shows brand driven growth.

pivots.from: Greplin, search across personal online accounts
pivots.to: Cue, a predictive personal assistant app showing your day
pivots.why: Moved from search to proactive assistant; the stated reason was not found

outcome_analysis: Greplin launched in 2010, raised 4 million dollars from Sequoia in February 2011, rebranded to Cue in June 2012 and was acquired by Apple in October 2013 for a reported 35 to 60 million dollars. Cue closed its service just before the deal, so the exit was effectively a team and technology acquisition for Apple's assistant efforts. The founders and Sequoia backing helped, but the product was shut down rather than scaled.
notes: The Wikipedia entry for Daniel Gross says Greplin raised 10 million dollars from Index in November 2012 but that snippet was truncated and the Cue page lists only the Sequoia round, so the Index round is unverified and not recorded. CB Insights total 4.72M. Apple price was never confirmed: sources range 35 to 45 million (AppleInsider tip) and 50 to 60 million (TechCrunch). The YC page lists founders differently from other sources; the Sequoia round stage label is not stated in the source so stage is other. Competitor entries come from search summaries, not full reads.
